takeaway: The recurrent laryngeal nerve (from the vagus) ascends in the tracheo-oesophageal groove and enters the larynx deep to the inferior border of the inferior constrictor.

question.text: Which statement regarding the recurrent laryngeal nerve, at risk in thyroid surgery, is true?

answer.text: It enters the larynx deep to the inferior border of the inferior constrictor of the pharynx.

lines.text: The recurrent laryngeal nerve is the structure to avoid in thyroid surgery.
It comes from the vagus nerve, not the hypoglossal.
It ascends in the groove between the trachea and the oesophagus, not descends.
On the left it hooks under the aortic arch, and on the right under the right subclavian artery.
Finally it reaches the larynx, passing deep to the inferior border of the inferior constrictor.
